Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize for caching and batching. Discussed cost model and POC scope.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, with Samir our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Elena: Hi Ava, doing well, thanks. Excited to see the Optimize walkthrough, our main goal is to understand how we can reduce per-token costs without blowing past our latency SLOs.
[00:22] Samir: Awesome. Quick agenda — we'll cover batching strategies, prefix vs KV cache, show a cost model for a typical NovaBank chat workload, and then propose a POC.
[00:35] Marcus: Quick callout — infra wise we're currently on k8s with GPU nodes in GCP, and we have SSO/SAML + KMS for keys. We also have strict data residency for EU customers.
[00:50] Priya: From security side, we'll need SOC2 evidence and details about audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:10] Ava: Noted. We'll share SOC2 and secure-architecture docs after the call.

[02:15] Samir: Ok jumping in. For batching, Redwood Optimize recommends dynamic batching windows. So rather than fixed 50ms windows, we look at traffic distribution. For chat workloads where there's a short user think-time, you can get 2-4x batching efficiency without impacting p95 too much.
[02:45] Elena: Hmm, can you quantify "2-4x" in cost terms?
[02:50] Samir: Yes — as a ballpark, in our example below we used a 12-token context prompt + 128-token generation. With no cache and minimal batching, cost per 1k requests was X. With workload-aware batching (target 20-40ms avg wait) you pick up about 30% token efficiency because you amortize KV cache and kernel warmups. And when you add prefix/KV caching the delta gets larger.
[03:30] Marcus: Sorry, X? that was a placeholder in the deck, what is the actual number?
[03:34] Samir: Right, sorry the slide had placeholders. In practical terms for our test harness: baseline model inference cost was roughly $0.90 per 1000 requests for the 7B-like model (generate ~128 tokens). When you optimize batching and enable KV cache with a 45% hit-rate, that drops to about $0.50 per 1000 — so roughly a 44% reduction. (numbers rounded)
[04:05] Priya: That seems significant. What's the hit-rate realistic assumption? 45% seems optimistic for banking dialogs.
[04:12] Samir: Good question. Hit-rate depends on how repetitive prefixes are. For templated flows like auth, balance queries, and FAQ it can be 40-60%. For open-ended support it will be lower. Our guidance: instrument for prefix frequency, start with conservative 20-30% for general chat, tune to as you collect telemetry.

[05:30] Ava: Also note we have two cache modes — prefix caching (shorter tokens cached by exact-match prefix) and KV cache (serialized key-value for attention state). Prefix is cheaper to index but less flexible; KV cache supports longer contexts and stateful sessions.
[05:52] Elena: Which one is better for our use-case? We have a lot of multi-turn banking sessions that reference previous account details.
[06:00] Samir: For multi-turn where you need to resume the KV cache gives better latency and correctness but needs more RAM per user. Prefix cache handles identical prefixes very cheaply. In NovaBank's case, a hybrid approach usually works — prefix cache for frequently repeated templates like greetings and menu options, KV cache for session continuation on authenticated flows.

[07:40] Samir: Walkthrough of cost model slide: assume 100k monthly active users, average 15 requests/day, avg generate tokens 100, baseline compute cost estimate (on Redwood-hosted dEDicated-like profile) was ~$18k/mo. With batching and a 35% KV cache hit-rate we eyeballed savings of ~$7k/mo. With aggressive tuning toward 50% hit-rate you can see ~50% savings. These are illustrative; we'll run an exact POC benchmark.
[08:30] Marcus: Are those numbers including extra RAM cost for KV cache? We worry about node sizing.
[08:35] Samir: Good call. The worksheet separates compute cost from memory overhead. KV cache memory is estimated as ~1.5KB per active session for our quantized runtimes (varies by model & sequence length). We include memory cost in dedicated sizing — that increases pod RAM requirements by ~20% in the example but still net positive because of reduced compute ops. We'll share the sizing spreadsheet.

[10:00] Elena: How does batching affect tail latency? Our p95 target for logged-in flows is 250ms.
[10:08] Samir: Batching trades throughput for a small added queueing delay. Redwood's Optimize looks at latency SLOs and will cap batch windows dynamically. For your 250ms SLO we typically configure a 15-25ms batching window with concurrency limits; this keeps p95 within target while improving throughput. We can show P95 numbers in the POC.

[12:30] Priya: KMS — how do you integrate customer KMS for key wrapping and model request encryption?
[12:38] Ava: We support customer-managed KMS in Private/Dedicated modes and can integrate HSM-backed keys for critical customers. We'll share the secure-arch doc and our audit log retention options.

[15:00] Samir: Demo time — I'll share my screen. (screen sharing) On the console we have the Optimize tab; you can toggle batching policy presets (aggressive, balanced, low-latency). Each preset shows estimated cost per million tokens and expected p95. Here I'm switching to "balanced" and we see an estimated 35% cost reduction vs baseline.
[15:45] Samir: Now the KV cache settings — you can set session TTL, max entries per node, and cache compression (we use a 4-bit quantized store to reduce memory). There's also an approximation for hit-rate; you can simulate workloads by pasting a small prompt corpus to get estimated hit rates.
[16:20] Elena: That simulate feature — is that sampling our real telemetry or synthetic?
[16:25] Samir: You can upload anonymized prefix logs or run a dry-run with a sample dataset. For privacy we recommend anonymizing PII before upload; in private deployments we can point to internal telemetry windows.

[18:40] Marcus: On the dedicated vs hosted question — we need predictability and data isolation, likely Dedicated. Will the batching and KV cache features behave the same on Dedicated?
[18:48] Ava: Yes, the same runtime and Optimize tooling are available on Dedicated. The difference is the capacity isolation and SLA. For Dedicated we provide autoscaling policies and burst pools.

[20:10] Samir: Back to numbers. Example scenario (slide): 100k MAU, avg 15 req/day, avg 100 tokens generated. Baseline token compute cost (no cache, minimal batching): $18,000/month. With batching + prefix/KV mixed cache at 35% hit-rate + standard compression: ~$11,000/month. Net savings: ~$7,000/mo. We also model larger models where savings scale linearly with token compute costs.
[21:00] Priya: I want the exact assumptions in a spreadsheet — model size, tokens-per-request, gpu type, reserved capacity discount.
[21:06] Ava: We'll send the full worksheet with reserved capacity pricing and sensitivity analysis.

[23:00] Elena: For the POC, what does Redwood need from us?
[23:06] Samir: Ideally: 1) a small representative prefix log (anonymized), 2) target latency SLOs, 3) expected MAU and burst patterns, 4) whitelisted IPs for private endpoints if you want on-prem / VPC. With that we'll run a bench with your workload and provide explicit savings and p95 numbers.
[23:40] Marcus: Timeline — we can deliver the logs and SLO doc by Friday Nov 13. Legal review for NDA is in-flight.

[25:10] Ava: Great. Quick deep-dive: cache eviction policy. For KV we support LRU + TTL; for prefix we support exact match and fuzzy-match (approx). Fuzzy matching increases hit-rate at slight risk of incorrect completions — we recommend using it for non-sensitive templates only.
[26:00] Elena: Could fuzzy matches cause hallucinations in transactional flows?
[26:06] Samir: Potentially — that's why we recommend keep transactional flows on KV cache or disabled fuzzy-match and do strict prefix matching for any flow that touches account numbers or balances.

[28:30] Samir: A note about quantization: enabling 4-bit int quantization reduces VM memory and inference ops and is compatible with our KV cache path; some tiny accuracy regression for specific tasks but usually negligible for templated conversations. We'll include evals for your prompts in the POC.

[31:00] Priya: On audit logs, do you include token-level logs or only request-level metadata? We need to know what you'd persist for compliance.
[31:08] Ava: By default we persist request-level metadata (timestamp, model, route, token counts). Token-level content logging is opt-in and should be configured per customer. For Private deployments you control retention policies.

[33:20] Elena: Any limitations on session length for KV cache? We have some sessions that go 2-3k tokens in history.
[33:28] Samir: KV cache scales with sequence length — memory grows with active past tokens. For very long histories we recommend summarization or periodic checkpointing to reduce active cache size. Practically, we cap per-session in our recommended default to 8k tokens, but configs can be adjusted if you accept memory tradeoffs.

[36:45] Marcus: For the POC run, can we test with our on-prem staging environment?
[36:50] Ava: Yes — we can run the POC in Dedicated or Private and install a small agent that proxies telemetry for simulation. We'll need network allowlists.

[39:10] Samir: Demoing the cost worksheet quickly — here's the sensitivity: if hit-rate goes from 20% to 40%, savings double-ish because you reduce the heavy generate ops. Also batching improvements compound with cache; they are not independent.
[40:00] Elena: Any gotchas on cold starts? We occasionally see high latency on new model versions after deploy.
[40:06] Samir: Cold-starts are why we recommend warmup policies — keep small pinned pools per route, and use prefix warming for expected heavy prefixes. We also support preheat jobs during deploys.

[42:00] Priya: From a legal/procurement perspective, what's typical contract length for Dedicated? 12 or 36 months?
[42:06] Ava: Typical is 12-36 months with discounts for longer commitments. We'll share committed capacity examples.

[45:20] Samir: Quick note on telemetry — Optimize exports per-route hit-rates, per-prefix frequency, and top offending prefixes. That data drives the tuning recommendations we put into the config.

[47:30] Marcus: If we choose Private, does your team handle the deployment or do we self-install?
[47:36] Ava: We have both models: managed Private installs (we run the control plane in your VPC) or self-host kits with partner support. We'll share the options and estimated timeline.

[50:00] Elena: Ok let's recap next steps — send pricing & secure docs, Samir to run cost estimate using our logs, schedule POC week of Nov 16.
[50:12] Ava: Correct, and we'll include a workbook with sensitivity to model size and reserved capacity discounts.

[51:00] Priya: One more question — do you support on-the-wire encryption end-to-end with customer keys?
[51:06] Samir: Yes, TLS + customer-managed KMS for key wrapping in Private/Dedicated.

[53:00] Ava: Any other questions?
[53:05] Elena: No, that's it. Thanks — this was helpful.
[53:10] Marcus: We'll get logs to you by Friday Nov 13.
